content.title: US IT hardware stocks tumble as Morgan Stanley flags slowing demand
content.summary: U.S. IT hardware stocks dropped on Tuesday after Morgan Stanley downgraded the sector, warning of ​slowing demand as companies rein in spending amid economic ‌uncertainty and rising component costs. The Wall Street brokerage said corporate technology leaders dialing back ‌hardware spending plans adds to existing concerns over higher input costs and supply bottlenecks, cutting its industry view to "cautious" from "in line." "A 'perfect storm' of slowing demand, input cost inflation and rich valuations is emerging, leading us ⁠to get more defensive ‌into 2026," the analysts wrote.
